title: Investigate Whether Safety Benchmark Scores Predict Real User Harm Reports

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The ecological validity gap between safety benchmarks and real-world harm is widely discussed conceptually. 'Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?' (Ren et al., arXiv:2407.21792, 2024) shows many safety benchmarks highly correlate with general capabilities rather than measuring safety independently. 'How Should AI Safety Benchmarks Benchmark Safety?' (arXiv:2601.23112, 2026) argues measurement validity erodes through proxy chains and that halving a toxicity score does not halve actual harm. 'Can We Trust AI Benchmarks?' (AIES 2025) documents the evaluation gap between pre-deployment tests and real-world outcomes. However, no published study has performed a direct rank-correlation analysis between published safety benchmark scores and real-world harm proxies (moderation actions, incident logs, red-team community reports). The conceptual critique is well-established but the empirical correlation study remains a gap, albeit constrained by data availability.
key_references: Ren et al. Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress? arXiv:2407.21792, 2024.

The narrow contribution — format sensitivity of safety evaluation rather than general task performance — retains partial novelty.

title: Multimodal Safety Benchmark: Table and Chart Injection Attacks

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multimodal safety attacks on VLMs are actively studied. FigStep (AAAI 2025 Oral) achieves 82.5% ASR via typographic visual prompts, and FigStep-Pro bypasses OCR detectors. MM-SafetyBench (ECCV 2024) evaluates safety across 13 scenarios with 5,040 text-image pairs. FC-Attack (arXiv:2502.21059, 2025) uses auto-generated flowcharts for jailbreaking. However, the specific attack surface of embedding harmful instructions in table/chart *metadata* (not typographic content in images, but structured data metadata) for code-interpreter and data analysis models is a distinct and less-explored vector. Most existing work focuses on image-level visual prompt injection rather than structured data metadata injection in analytical workflows.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The effect of temperature on safety has been noted in safety evaluation literature. The general direction (temperature affects safety) is known, but quantifying which hazard categories are most temperature-sensitive on a standard benchmark is a useful and partially novel contribution.

title: Benchmark for Permission Escalation Detection in Multi-Agent Systems

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 names Identity and Privilege Abuse as a critical risk, noting agents can escalate privileges by abusing identity or inheriting credentials. NeuralTrust, Lasso Security, and Practical DevSecOps have analyzed these risks conceptually. Insecure Inter-Agent Communication (ASI07) is documented as enabling spoofed messages. The OWASP framework identifies the risk category but does not provide evaluation benchmarks. Creating a concrete, reusable benchmark for permission escalation detection in multi-agent systems addresses a clear gap between risk identification and empirical evaluation.
